items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Art Hodes and his trio have opened at Jimmy Ryan's at 52nd Street. And he's featuring Danny Alvin and Mezzrow, real good music.

ctx.x:
Well, it's like the New Yorker, it has -- mostly for music. But the type in the New Yorker is large enough that you don't need glasses. The type in Cue was very small, very -- you had to almost glare at it at a short distance.

Now, it was after work, I found a restuarant that's

open, a one-armed joint, and I'm sitting at the counter and I order the -- I'm a little stoned, I've been working all night. And I'm sitting there looking at that writeup, it says, Art Hodes and his trio have opened at Jimmy Ryan's at 52nd Street. And he's featuring Danny Alvin and Mezzrow, real good music.

And I'm reading it and reading it and reading it. I must have -- I don't know how long I'm in there. I must have been there at least 45 minutes. And suddenly the place is swarming with police. And it seems that while I was reading this writeup, some character -- and I heard somebody come in, came and sat way down at the end of the counter, got something to eat and as he walked out to pay the bill, there were some billboards between the cash register and the window. So that the outside people couldn't see in so…
